stimuli.text:
A `Thermostat` keeps a temperature setting between a minimum and a maximum, inclusive.


• `Thermostat(int min, int max, int start)` creates a thermostat. Precondition: min <= start <= max.

• `void raise(int amount)` and `void lower(int amount)` change the setting by amount, but never past max or min.

• `int getSetting()` returns the current setting.

• `int getChanges()` returns how many calls to raise or lower actually changed the setting.

Example:

```java
Thermostat t = new Thermostat(14, 30, 28);
t.raise(5);      // setting is 30
t.raise(1);      // still 30: no change
t.lower(4);      // setting is 26
t.getSetting();  // returns 26
t.getChanges();  // returns 2
```

options.text: Share the locations with more teachers
options.why: Wider access increases privacy risk.

options.text: Record only whether each student is on campus, not exact locations
options.why: Correct. Collecting only the data needed reduces privacy risk.

options.text: Store the exact locations in a larger database
options.why: More storage does not reduce what is collected.

questions.explanation: Collecting only the data needed reduces privacy risk.
